descriptionChirho: Piel intensive active meaning 'to tear apart, snap off, or break' bonds, cords, or fetters by force, used of breaking restraints and severing ties in Judg 16:9, 16:12; Ps 2:3, 107:14; Isa 58:6; Jer 2:20, 5:5, 30:8; Nah 1:13. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'snapped/break/tore off,' Kor 'kkeun-eotda' (broke), Hin 'toda' (broke), Spa 'rompio/rompamos.'

Piel form with the nuance of uprooting or pulling up from a fixed position, such as tent pegs, plants, or structures from the ground, in Ezek 17:9 and 23:34. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'pull-up/tear,' Kor 'ppob-a-naerira/jjij-eurira' (uproot/tear), Hin 'ukharega/nochegi' (will uproot/will tear), Spa 'arrancara/arrancaras.'

Nifal passive meaning 'to be broken or snapped,' said of cords, ropes, bonds, or threads that give way under strain, in Judg 16:9; Job 17:11; Eccl 4:12; Isa 5:27, 33:20; Jer 10:20. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'snaps/are broken/is broken,' Kor 'kkeun-ginda/kkeun-eojyeotda' (snaps/were broken), Hin 'TuTta hai/TuT gayin' (snaps/were broken), Spa 'se rompe/fueron rotos.'

Nifal passive meaning 'to be uprooted, torn out, or pulled away from a fixed place,' of tent pegs, roots, or persons separated from their position, in Josh 4:18; Job 18:14; Jer 6:29. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'were-lifted/is torn/are separated,' Kor 'ddeonassda/kkeun-eojirira' (departed/torn), Hin 'ukhade/ukhara jaega' (uprooted/will be uprooted), Spa 'arrancaron/sera arrancado.'

Qal active and Hifil causative meaning 'to draw away or pull persons from a position, to lure troops out' as a military stratagem or metaphorical uprooting. In Josh 8:6 and Judg 20:32 Israel lures enemies away; in Jer 12:3 the prophet asks God to 'pull them out'; in Jer 22:24 and Lev 22:24. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'drawn them away/pull them out/tear you off,' Kor 'kkeul-eo-naegi/kkeul-eo-naesoseo' (to lure out), Hin 'khinchenge/khinch le' (will draw/pull), Spa 'alejemos/arrancalos.'

Hofal and Nifal passive meaning 'to be drawn away or lured out,' the passive counterpart of the active 'draw away' sense, describing persons or troops who have been enticed from their position, in Josh 8:16 and Judg 20:31. Multilingual glosses: Eng 'were drawn away,' Kor 'kkeun-eojyeotda/kkeullyeotda' (were broken off/were lured), Hin 'khinche gaye' (were drawn), Spa 'fueron alejados/fueron atraidos.'
